title: Hydrophobic Salt-modified Nafion for Enzyme Immobilization and Stabilization
protocol: Shake a bottle of 5% w/v Nafion suspension vigorously for approximately 30 seconds.
Pipette out 2 mL of re-suspended Nafion into a glass vial.
Measure a 3-fold molar excess of alkyl ammonium bromide salt relative to the sulfonic acid groups on the Nafion polymer and add it to the vial.
Vortex the vial at 1500 rpm for 10-15 minutes.
Pour the viscous solution into a plastic weighing tray measuring approximately 3 x 3 inches.
Transfer any residual solution from the vial to the weighing tray using a pipette.
Allow the solvents to evaporate from the weigh boat, taking more than 6 hours for complete evaporation.
Cover the weigh boat and soak in 18M Ωcm de-ionized water (10-20 mL) for 12-24 hours.
Pour out the soaking solution after the incubation period.
Rinse the tray with DI water three times, ensuring careful handling to avoid losing any polymer film.
Allow the weighing tray to sit uncovered until the polymer is completely dry.
Carefully remove the dried film from the weighing tray using a spatula.
Transfer the dried film into a clean glass vial.
Add 2 mL of ethanol and 3 ceramic mixing beads to the vial.
Vortex for 4 hours or until the polymer film is completely re-suspended.
Weigh out 1-10 mg of the enzyme into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
For an enzyme in solution, use a BCA assay to determine protein amount.
Add an appropriate amount of 100 mM phosphate buffer to bring the protein concentration to 1-10 mg/mL.
To 120 μL of the 1 mg/mL enzyme solution, add 60 μL of alkyl ammonium-modified Nafion solution.
Vortex for 10 seconds.
Pipette 60 μL of the enzyme/polymer solution into the bottom of 3 separate 1 cm² cuvettes.
Allow the enzyme/polymer solution to dry overnight.
Add 1.3 mL of 50 mM sodium pyrophosphate (pH 8.8) to the cuvette.
Add 1.5 mL of 15 mM NAD (freshly prepared) to the cuvette.
Add 0.1 mL water to the cuvette.
Place the cuvette in a UV/Vis spectrophotometer set to a wavelength of 340 nm.
Zero the spectrometer.
Add 0.1 mL ethanol to the cuvette.
Mix the reagents by gently pipetting the solution up and down 5 times.
For a blank, use 0.1 mL of additional water instead of the 0.1 mL of ethanol.
Record the absorbance at 340 nm at 5 minutes after the reagents were added to the cuvette.
Record the absorbance at 340 nm at 20 minutes after the reagents were added to the cuvette.
Plot the two data points to get a slope that can be used for activity calculations.
Add 1.5 mL of sodium phosphate (pH 7.3) to the cuvette.
Add 200 μL of 600 μM PMS to the cuvette.
Place the cuvette in a UV/Vis spectrophotometer set to a wavelength of 600 nm.
Zero the spectrometer.
Add 100 μL of 700 μL DCIP to the cuvette.
Add 200 μL of the substrate of interest (ethanol, acetaldehyde, glycerol, glucose, or glyceraldehyde) to the cuvette.
Mix the reagents by gently pipetting the solution up and down 5 times.
For a blank, use 200 μL of water instead of the substrate of interest.
Record the absorbance at 600 nm at 5 minutes after the reagents were added to the cuvette.
Record the absorbance at 600 nm at 20 minutes after the reagents were added to the cuvette.
Add 2.0 mL of solution containing 0.2 M p-hydroxybenzoic acid, 0.02 % (w/v) sodium azide, 128 U peroxidase, 0.3 mM 4-aminoantipyrine, 1 M potassium phosphate, and 50 mM glucose to the cuvette.
Mix the solution by pipetting up and down 5 times.
Place the cuvette in a UV/Vis spectrophotometer set to a wavelength of 510 nm.
Record the absorbance at 510 nm at 5 minutes after adding reagents to the cuvette.
Record the absorbance at 510 nm again at 20 minutes after adding reagents to the cuvette.
Mix modified Nafion polymer and enzyme.
Co-cast the mixture onto the bottom of a cuvette.
Conduct enzymatic activity assays to assess enzyme stability within the polymer film.
Compare enzyme activity in immobilized form within modified Nafion films versus buffer solution.
